brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0) with a flat top, capped and joint-bolted. It is a small shelf, not sized or checked for a stack of books.
Two notch drawers, one in each notch beside the bases (notch:0#0,1#notch1 and notch:0#1,-1#notch4). The BOM lists 2 drawer bodies with lids and runners. The configurator reports meshClash clear.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It has no load ratings, and the material is unknown, so I can't claim 50 kg. Test the printed unit yourself before loading it. Don't assume it carries that weight.

finish.summary: I built a small two-base shelf with two notch drawers, end caps and locked joints. The configurator reports no collisions. I can't verify the 50 kg rating, so that requirement is unmet. The unit may also tip, because the configurator raised a STABILITY_TIP warning when I placed the first drawer frame. I did not clear it.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
